prose: Facebook co-founder Chris Hughes proposes in the Financial Times an 'Office of AI Supervision': a regulator that would embed dedicated teams inside the frontier AI labs themselves, with staff serving a three-year term designed to avoid regulatory capture. The model borrows from resident-inspector regimes - supervision from inside the building rather than after-the-fact document requests. The article is paywalled, so this summary is based on the headline and lead captured by the feed.
highlights: Chris Hughes proposes an 'Office of AI Supervision'.
Teams embedded inside frontier AI labs.
Three-year terms to blunt regulatory capture.
Resident-inspector model rather than after-the-fact requests.
FT piece paywalled; summary from headline/lead.
